name: Shaista Khan
seoTitle: Shaista Khan in Bengal: Subahdar and Chittagong Campaign
seoDescription: Shaista Khan governed Bengal from 1664 to 1688, reorganised Mughal administration, and directed the campaign that captured Chittagong in 1666.
role: Mughal subahdar of Bengal and imperial commander
contribution: Shaista Khan became Bengal's subahdar after Mir Jumla's death and governed for the longest tenure of any Mughal provincial governor there. He tightened administrative discipline, worked through a network of district officials and family commanders, and planned the combined land-and-naval campaign that captured Chittagong in January 1666.
context: Seventeenth-century Mughal Bengal, where Arakanese raids and Portuguese piracy threatened the coastal frontier, while the provincial government sought tighter control over river routes, ports, trade, and revenue administration.
impact: The Chittagong campaign, led in the field by his son Buzurg Umed Khan with naval support, ended Arakanese control of the port and brought it into the Mughal province under the name Islamabad. His building activity in Dhaka, including Chhota Katra, also reflects the capital's commercial and administrative growth during his tenure.
highlight: Shaista Khan combined administrative consolidation in Bengal with the 1666 Mughal conquest of Chittagong.
